findings.issue_text: pkg/plugins/log/fake.go:46 — [P1/99] `func (f *TestLogger) FromContext(_ context.Context) Logger { return NewTestLogger() }`: this stand-in violates the new Logger contract by returning a different logger instead of the receiver plus context; LoggerMiddleware now writes completion events to that unobservable instance, so every caller injecting TestLogger loses its recorded log event.

pkg/plugins/log/ifaces.go:23 — [P1/92] `FromContext(ctx context.Context) Logger`: adding a required method to the exported Logger interface is a source-incompatible API change; every downstream/custom Logger implementation now fails to satisfy Logger, turning a middleware rename into a consumer-wide compile break.

pkg/plugins/log/ifaces.go:23 — [P1/100] `FromContext(ctx context.Context) Logger`: the rename expands the public `plugins/log.Logger` contract, forcing every external implementation to add a method and changing the integration surface; the task states only a middleware rename, with no acceptance of this breaking API change.

pkg/services/pluginsintegration/pluginsintegration.go:160 — [P2/100] `clientmiddleware.NewContextualLoggerMiddleware(),`: the change inserts a new request-context logging stage that propagates plugin, datasource, endpoint, and user attributes beyond the renamed metrics middleware; no task or review artifact records acceptance of this added logging behavior.

pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/metrics_middleware.go:146 — [P1/90] `for _, v := range req.Queries {`: a nil `*backend.QueryDataRequest` now dereferences and panics before delegation; `CreateMiddlewares` installs MetricsMiddleware ahead of the existing LoggerMiddleware, whose explicit `if req == nil { return m.next.QueryData(ctx, req) }` previously preserves pass-through, so a malformed/optional request crashes the request path instead of reaching the client/error handler.

pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/metrics_middleware_test.go:85 — [P2/88] `require.NoError(t, tc.fn(cdt))`: every new middleware test exercises only the success path, so a regression in `instrumentPluginRequest` that emits `statusError`/`statusCancelled` incorrectly (or fails to record those request metrics) remains untested even though those changed error branches affect observability for failed and canceled plugin calls.

pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/metrics_middleware_test.go:33 — [P2/82] `t.Run("should instrument requests", func(t *testing.T) {`: the added test validates metrics middleware only; it never invokes the newly inserted contextual-logger middleware or observes the context received by `next`, so regressions that omit or mislabel endpoint/plugin/datasource/user attributes will still pass while the refactor has moved those attributes out of `LoggerMiddleware`.

goldens.comment: The ContextualLoggerMiddleware methods (QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth, CollectMetrics) panic when a nil request is received. This occurs because they directly access req.PluginContext (via the instrumentContext function) without first checking if req is nil. This is a regression, as previous middleware layers gracefully handled nil requests.

The traceID is no longer logged for plugin requests. During a refactoring, the tracing import and the logic to extract and add traceID from the context to log parameters were removed from the LoggerMiddleware. The newly introduced ContextualLoggerMiddleware does not add this information, resulting in missing traceID in plugin request logs and impacting debugging and request tracing capabilities.

The `TestLogger.FromContext` method returns a new `TestLogger` instance via `NewTestLogger()` instead of returning the receiver (f). This causes logs to be recorded on an un-referenced instance, leading to broken test assertions that expect logs to be recorded on the original logger.

The MetricsMiddleware behavior of iterating over req.Queries is consistent with expecting valid requests, same as the existing code patterns.

The MetricsMiddleware (renamed from InstrumentationMiddleware) at line 141 in metrics_middleware.go shows QueryData iterating over req.Queries, but there's no evidence in the diff that LoggerMiddleware ever had a 'if req == nil' check that protected against nil requests.
